add.title: Ghana parliament passes bill criminalising gay acts
add.summary: BBC (30 May 2026): Ghana's parliament approved a new bill criminalising homosexuality and the promotion of LGBTQ+ activities; it proposes that identifying as lesbian, gay, bisexual, transgender or queer be punished by up to three years' imprisonment, adds a 'duty to report' prohibited acts to police, and was passed under pressure from religious leaders on President Mahama, whose ratification is still required. Establishes the direct state pathway by which trans people in Ghana can be imprisoned for identity alone - the population to which any prison-placement practice would apply - while containing no provision on how such prisoners would be housed.

add.title: People 'panicking' as Ghana passes sweeping law criminalising LGBTQ+ activity
add.summary: The Guardian (1 Jun 2026): the Human Sexual Rights and Family Values Bill, passed by Ghana's parliament on 29 May 2026 and expected to be signed by President Mahama, mandates prison sentences of three to 10 years - up to three years for identifying as LGBTQ+ and longer for promotion/advocacy. Community groups (e.g. One Love Sisters Ghana) report panic, eviction risk and self-censorship. The article contains no information on prison placement of trans prisoners, confirming the absence of any publicly documented housing policy for them in Ghana.
